title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023
purpose: Replaced the 163-year-old Indian Penal Code (IPC) with a modern criminal legal code focused on justice rather than colonial punishment.
scope: Applies across all states and Union Territories of India for criminal offences.
importantConcepts: Introduction of Community Service as a statutory punishment for minor offences.
Categorization of Organized Crime, Gangrape, Mob Lynching, and Terrorist Acts.
Gender-neutral provisions for offences against children and property.
Scrapping of Sedition (Section 124A IPC) replaced by treasonous acts against Sovereignty (Section 152 BNS).
practicalRelevance: Every criminal charge, FIR, and trial initiated after July 1, 2024 is registered under BNS sections instead of IPC sections.
officialRef: Ministry of Law and Justice, Gazette Notification 2023

title: Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023
purpose: Governs the procedural framework for police investigations, arrests, bail, trials, and court administration in criminal matters.
scope: All criminal investigations and court proceedings in India.
importantConcepts: Mandatory forensic investigation for offences punishable by 7+ years imprisonment.
Strict timelines: Charge sheets within 90 days; trial judgments within 45 days of conclusion.
Statutory recognition of Zero FIR, e-FIR, and digital/audio-video recording of searches and seizures.
Enhanced safeguards for arrests of elderly or infirm citizens.
practicalRelevance: Defines police powers, bail application procedure (Sec 478-496), FIR filing rules (Sec 173), and Magistrate jurisdictions.

title: Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023
purpose: Modernizes the rules of evidence admissibility, giving equal legal standing to electronic records, digital signatures, and server logs.
scope: All judicial proceedings in or before any court in India.
importantConcepts: Electronic & Digital Records recognized as primary evidence.
Standardized admissibility for cloud storage, emails, WhatsApp logs, and smartphone recordings.
Protection of spousal communication and legal professional privilege.
practicalRelevance: Crucial for establishing guilt or innocence in court trials through physical and digital evidence.

title: Constitution of India
purpose: The supreme legal document establishing the political structure, fundamental rights, directive principles, and duties of citizens and government.
importantConcepts: Part III: Fundamental Rights (Articles 12 to 35) ensuring equality, freedom, protection against exploitation, and constitutional remedies.
Articles 32 & 226: Power of Supreme Court and High Courts to issue Writs (Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, etc.).
Preamble: Declares India a Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic Republic.
practicalRelevance: Any state law or executive action that violates Fundamental Rights can be struck down as unconstitutional.
